standard.title: The crosswalk tool's own contract, mapped to the tests that hold it
standard.scope_note: Not a regulation. This file exists so the COVERED path has at least one real customer: a clause whose probe genuinely runs and passes. Keeping it separate from the MDR file avoids inflating a regulatory crosswalk with self-tests.

rows.id: TC-1 three-state decision is a pure function
TC-2 a declared gap stays green and is counted
TC-3 an unproven claim turns the run red

rows.reason: CI now runs the same command - tools/recheck.py - on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, so all six probe strings are executed under POSIX sh and cmd.exe, and recheck exits 3 if either platform produces different bytes. Before this job existed, the Windows runner only ran static tests (evaluate(run=False)), so nothing in CI had ever executed a probe string under cmd.exe - which is the opposite of what this reason used to claim. What is still missing: macOS, and any shell that is neither posix-sh nor cmd.exe; quoting there is untested, and this probe reads the workflow rather than exercising those shells.
